brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Keep sewing supplies tidy: separate places for different items
requirements.evidence: Nine sections to keep supplies apart: the plain bin bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full suits fabric or a tape measure; the 2-way bin bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 suits thread or markers; the 3-way bin bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 and the 3-way pocket notch:0#1,1#notch2 suit small notions like pins and buttons.

capOpenFaces closes every open face with end caps (10 caps), and lockJoints bolts the three cells together (3 joint bolts). The final check passed and found no parts colliding. This only covers fit; the build hasn't been checked for strength.

finish.summary: I built a small tabletop organiser for sewing supplies. It's three hex cells in a cluster, each holding a full-depth bin (one plain, one split into 2 compartments, one split into 3), plus a 3-compartment pocket bin in the gap where two cells meet. That gives 9 sections in all: 1 large, 2 medium and 6 small (3 in the bin, 3 in the pocket). All open faces are capped and the joints are bolted together, which brings it to 17 parts, about 1,786 g of filament and 2,425 print minutes. The final check passed with no issues and no parts colliding. There are no sewing items among the display props, so the bins are staged with similar small things: a tape measure, a marker, a pen and tweezers. They only show the scale; they aren't part of the build.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
